purpose: Test whether state security regeneration and administrative rebuilding change the effectiveness and durability of underground-network disruption against a reproductively live synthetic insurgency.
scientific_question: Do security presence and administrative reach complement underground disruption by building the intelligence penetration required to suppress rooted insurgent organization, and does any suppression persist after the intervention ends?

mechanism_hypotheses.H1: Turning on underground disruption should reduce rooted armed membership and recruitment hazard when intelligence penetration is nontrivial.
mechanism_hypotheses.H2: Security and administrative surges should increase the intelligence-penetration pathway and may make underground disruption more effective than the sum of separate effects.
mechanism_hypotheses.H3: If intervention-end suppression disappears after all factor surges are removed, the model exhibits temporary pressure rather than durable state recovery.
mechanism_hypotheses.H4: Fielded-force reduction without corresponding rooted-membership/recruitment reduction is not sufficient evidence of organizational suppression.

S_security_surge.high: 2x security recruitment rate, 2x training rate, 1.5x police target population fraction, 1.25x military personnel target

U_underground_disruption.high: underground disruption rate = SimulationConfig default (0.002/day) during intervention

design.post_intervention: At day 240 every cell restores the same baseline configuration, including zero underground disruption, and runs to day 360.

baseline_persistence_preflight.failure_rule: If any threshold fails, do not run or inspect factor-cell outcomes. Register a new support-regime preflight before changing challenge support.

primary_estimands: Within-seed S, A, and U main effects at day 240 and day 360.
Within-seed SxA, SxU, AxU, and SxAxU factorial interactions at day 240 and day 360.
U marginal effect separately in each S/A stratum, especially on rooted membership, recruitment hazard, intelligence penetration, and cumulative underground disruption.
For each nonbaseline cell, cell-minus-baseline effect at day 240 and day 360.
interpretation_rules: Negative interactions on lower-is-suppression insurgent outcomes indicate more-than-additive suppression; positive interactions do not.
A state-capacity pathway change is mechanistic support, not proof of mediation unless the linked insurgent outcome changes in the predicted direction.
Do not call a policy package universally superior and do not combine outcomes into one utility score.
Canonical and whole-insurgent-ecosystem outcomes must be reported together.
All claims describe mechanisms of the implemented synthetic model, not real-world operational prescriptions.
